description: Hi, I’m Santi. I’m 11 years old and am finishing the 5th grade—I’ll be moving on to the 6th grade soon! I’m really interested in astrology and everything related to space; I’d love to work at NASA and further my knowledge. I enjoy basketball and playing Minecraft. I’m very creative, intelligent, and have a great capacity for learning.
summary: We developed an interactive game for children aged 4 to 12, in which players can explore the various components required for a space mission—such as weight, energy, scientific data, and budget, among others. The game invites players to choose from three different components to help improve their mission. The goal is to engage children in this challenge, allowing them to learn about the fundamental requirements for a space mission as they assemble a rocket.
details:
This game was developed in Scratch. You must choose what type of astronaut you want to be and select the mission you wish to undertake—whether it’s exploring Earth or outer space. Then, in the workshop, you need to select the device best suited to the mission's requirements to ensure a successful outcome. To learn the rules, click on the astronaut. There is also a minigame where you can dodge asteroids and earn points by collecting the appropriate devices for each mission. In this minigame, you use the arrow keys on your computer.

This game aims to teach children who play it about various components required for a special mission—such as energy, scientific instruments, rocket capacity, spacecraft weight, and the necessary budget—so that the mission they choose can be successfully completed.
